name: @carlwr/zshref-mcp

tools.name: zsh_docs
tools.description:
Render markdown for a zsh token or canonical id from the bundled static zsh-5.9 reference.

Omitting `category` can return multiple matches for overlapping syntax.

Resolvers normalize input forms to canonical records (per-category, rule-based):

  INPUT:            RESOLVED:
                    category  id
  ----------        --------  --------
  ALIASES           option    aliases
  NO_ALIASES        option    aliases  (input-negated)
  -J                option    autocd
  +J                option    autocd   (input-negated)
  %number           job_spec  %number
  %1                job_spec  %number

Input `key` and the returned `id` may therefore differ; `id` fed back as `key`, with its `category`, returns exactly that record. `id` is shell-safe (printable ASCII, no whitespace).

Output object properties:
  matches[]          matched records
  matchesReturned    returned match count
  matchesTotal       total match count

  Each matches[] element — always:
    category           doc category
    id                 canonical id
    display            zsh-facing name
    title              record heading (markdown; not repeated in mdBody)
    mdBody             rendered markdown (empty for a record without prose)

  — when applicable:
    subKind            category facet (categories that have one)
    feedback           lossy-resolution signal (`kind`, e.g. `input-negated`)

No matches is not an error: matches[] is empty, matchesTotal is 0.

No shell execution, no environment access.

key.description:
zsh token or canonical id (lookup key)

Accepts: raw zsh tokens (`AUTO_CD`, `[[`, `%1`, `<<<`, `> word`) and canonical ids, with their `category`, from prior `zsh_search` / `zsh_list` (`autocd`).

category.description:
restrict to one doc category

With a category set, at most one match is returned.

If omitted, all categories are tried in the order given below, yielding at most one match per category.

Valid values:

  value
  -----
  complex_command       complex command
  reserved_word         reserved word
  precmd_modifier       precommand modifier
  builtin               builtin
  conditional_op        conditional operator
  special_function      special function
  special_param         special parameter
  process_subst         process substitution
  param_expn            parameter-expansion form
  param_expn_flag       parameter-expansion flag
  subscript_flag        parameter-subscript flag
  glob_flag             glob flag
  glob_qualifier        glob qualifier
  glob_op               glob operator
  history_expn          history-expansion component
  prompt_escape         prompt escape
  job_spec              job spec
  zle_widget            ZLE widget
  keymap                ZLE keymap
  arith_op              arithmetic operator
  mathfunc              math function
  option                option
  redirection           redirection
  comp_utility          completion utility

tools.name: zsh_search
tools.description:
Find candidate records in the bundled static zsh-5.9 reference by id/display heading.

Resolvers normalize input forms to canonical records (per-category, rule-based):

  INPUT:            RESOLVED:
                    category  id
  ----------        --------  --------
  ALIASES           option    aliases
  NO_ALIASES        option    aliases  (input-negated)
  -J                option    autocd
  +J                option    autocd   (input-negated)
  %number           job_spec  %number
  %1                job_spec  %number

Ranking:
  1. exact id/display
  2. resolver match
  3. prefix
  4. fuzzy score

Each matches[] element — always:
  category           doc category
  id                 canonical id
  display            zsh-facing name
  score              1 for exact/resolver/prefix; in (0,1) for fuzzy

— when applicable:
  subKind            category facet (categories that have one)

No markdown body. Use `zsh_docs` for full docs.

To enumerate without a query, use `zsh_list`.

No shell execution, no environment access.

query.description:
search string matched against ids and display headings

Empty or whitespace returns no matches; use `zsh_list` to enumerate.

category.description:
restrict to one doc category

If omitted, all categories are included.

Valid values:

  value
  -----
  complex_command       complex command
  reserved_word         reserved word
  precmd_modifier       precommand modifier
  builtin               builtin
  conditional_op        conditional operator
  special_function      special function
  special_param         special parameter
  process_subst         process substitution
  param_expn            parameter-expansion form
  param_expn_flag       parameter-expansion flag
  subscript_flag        parameter-subscript flag
  glob_flag             glob flag
  glob_qualifier        glob qualifier
  glob_op               glob operator
  history_expn          history-expansion component
  prompt_escape         prompt escape
  job_spec              job spec
  zle_widget            ZLE widget
  keymap                ZLE keymap
  arith_op              arithmetic operator
  mathfunc              math function
  option                option
  redirection           redirection
  comp_utility          completion utility

limit.description:
limit the number of matches to return

Use 0 for the total count only (no matches).

Default: 20

tools.name: zsh_list
tools.description:
Return id/display records from the bundled static zsh reference.

Identifiers only. Use `zsh_docs` for rendered markdown.

Order:
  category omitted: default category order
  category set: that category's record order

Each matches[] element — always:
  category           doc category
  id                 canonical id
  display            zsh-facing name

— when applicable:
  subKind            category facet (categories that have one)

No shell execution, no environment access.

instructions:
Tool → intent:
  `zsh_docs`   → look up docs for a zsh key (raw token or canonical id)
  `zsh_search` → fuzzy-match on tokens/ids → returns ids
  `zsh_list`   → enumerate records         → returns ids

  (feed search/list `id` back to `zsh_docs` as `key`, with its `category`)
